data_point: Raised Series C or later, or publicly traded
run_when: Code found a Series C+ mention, a stock ticker or an investor relations page; or the company is funded (investors named, SEC Form D, YC) but no pre-seed to Series B stage is confirmed.

prompt.task: Decide whether THIS company has raised a Series C or later round, or is publicly traded.
prompt.definition: Exclusions need positive evidence. Never exclude on an inference, an estimate or missing information. Requires a confirmed round, an IPO or an explicit public statement.
yes_when: The company says it raised a Series C, D or later round
The company shows its own stock ticker or says it is publicly traded
The company confirms a single funding round of $100 million or more, or a valuation of $1 billion or more (a stated fact, so it counts even when the round's letter isn't named)
no_when: The text confirms the latest round is Series B or earlier
unknown_when: Only size, polish or customer logos suggest the company is large
A Series C is mentioned but it may be another company's
watch_out_for: A company that merely looks large or mature is not excluded
Total raised across all rounds is not one round: only a single round of $100M+ or a $1B+ valuation counts
A subsidiary of a public company: answer 'unknown' and explain in the reason

evidence_quote.description: Exact words copied from the text. Empty when the answer is unknown.

source.description: Page name or URL the quote came from.

reason.description: One plain sentence explaining the answer.

web_search.note: An exclusion found on the web counts only with high confidence and an entity match by domain.

examples.input_excerpt: Pilot has raised over $150M in Series A, Series B, and Series C financing from Sequoia, Index Ventures

output.evidence_quote: Pilot has raised over $150M in Series A, Series B, and Series C financing
output.reason: The company states it raised a Series C.
